svg.title: Seizing a phone and searching a phone are different questions under Riley v. California
svg.desc: Officers may seize and secure a phone incident to arrest without a warrant. They generally may not search the digital contents of that phone without one, per the unanimous 2014 Supreme Court decision in Riley v. California. The warrant requirement protects what is stored on the device, but it does not return the device, so footage that exists only on the phone is out of reach either way.
svg.text: Two different questions, two different answers

Neither officer safety nor risk of evidence
The warrant rule protects what is stored on the phone. It does not put the phone back in your hand, and it does nothing at all about a phone dropped, smashed or wiped.
